diagnostics.title: Cost taken from resource assignments
diagnostics.detail: Activity-level cost fields are all zero in this export; earned value is computed from the resource assignments instead.

insights.title: Dangling logic
insights.finding: 5 activities have a start or finish that nothing controls, even though they do have relationships.
insights.recommendation: An activity whose successors are all SS can slip its finish forever without moving anything downstream. Add the missing FS/FF link so both ends of the activity are tied into the network.

insights.title: Out-of-sequence progress
insights.finding: 4 open activities have progressed against logic that is still waiting on its predecessor.
insights.recommendation: P6 holds their remaining work behind a link the site has already ignored, so the forecast is wrong. Change each link to the relationships the work actually followed - Repair XER does this - or re-plan the sequence.

insights.title: High float caused by missing successors
insights.finding: 1 activities combine float above 44 days with no successor at all.
insights.recommendation: This float is an artefact of missing logic, not real slack - the activity simply floats to the end of the project. Add the successor that reflects what the work actually enables.

insights.title: Remaining work with no resources or cost
insights.finding: 3 incomplete activities carry neither resources nor cost.
insights.recommendation: This work is invisible to earned value and to any resource histogram, so forecasts understate what is left to do. Load them, or exclude them from the EVM basis deliberately.

insights.title: Work recorded out of sequence
insights.finding: 29 relationships were broken by work that has since caught up - the successor started or finished before the logic allowed.
insights.recommendation: These no longer move any date, so they do not affect the forecast. They matter for as-built and delay analysis, where the logic should describe how the work was really done. Repair XER can re-type them to the relationships the actual dates satisfy.

checks.name: Logic
checks.description: Activities with no predecessor and/or no successor. Open ends let work float free of the network.

checks.name: Leads (negative lag)
checks.description: Negative lag lets a successor start before its predecessor finishes, compressing the path artificially.

checks.name: Lags
checks.description: Lags hide real work or float inside a relationship instead of modelling it as an activity. DCMA counts every positive lag; the lag setting on the Dashboard can raise the bar for comparison.
checks.threshold: ≤ 5% of relationships into incomplete work with any positive lag

checks.name: Relationship types
checks.description: Finish-to-Start should dominate. Heavy SS/FF/SF use makes the network harder to trace and often masks true drivers.
checks.note: Counted on 27 relationships into incomplete work, as DCMA does; links into finished work no longer drive anything.

checks.name: Hard constraints
checks.description: Constraints that fix a date rather than letting logic drive it can conceal negative float.
checks.note: Counts the DCMA list: Mandatory Start/Finish, Start/Finish On and Start/Finish On or Before. 0 other constraints present (not counted).

checks.name: High float
checks.description: Very large float usually means missing successor logic rather than genuine schedule slack.

checks.name: Negative float
checks.description: Any negative float means the current plan cannot meet its dates or constraints.

checks.name: High duration
checks.description: Long activities hide progress detail and make status reporting coarse. Measured on original duration.

checks.name: Invalid dates
checks.description: Actual dates cannot be in the future, and work not yet done cannot be forecast to start or finish in the past.
checks.note: Forecast dates are P6's early dates from the last reschedule. If they are in the past, the file was not rescheduled after statusing - press F9 in P6 and export again.

checks.name: Resources / cost loading
checks.description: Activities without resources or cost cannot contribute to earned value.

checks.name: Missed activities
checks.description: Activities planned to complete before the data date that finished late or are still open.
checks.note: Measured against P6's planned dates (the target dates in the export), the usual stand-in when the file does not carry its baseline.

checks.name: Critical path test
checks.description: Adding 600 days to the longest critical activity must push the project finish by the same amount. If it does not, the critical path is broken.
checks.note: Tested on 'A1390' (longest activity on the recomputed critical path). Passes if at least 95% of the injected delay reaches the finish, or if the delayed activity still drives the completion activity afterwards.

checks.name: Critical Path Length Index (CPLI)
checks.description: (critical path length + total float) / critical path length. Below 1.0 means the remaining path cannot absorb any delay.
checks.note: Critical path length 161 working days; total float -3 days (lowest float of any open activity - the file's stored dates were not produced by a reschedule, so the finishing activity's stored float cannot be relied on).

checks.name: Baseline Execution Index (BEI)
checks.description: Activities actually completed divided by activities planned to be complete by the data date.
checks.note: 33 completed vs 36 planned complete. Start execution index 1.000 (39 of 39 started). Measured against P6's planned dates.
